title: Automated FIB Cross-Sectioning for 3D SIMS: Local Volume and Global Volume 7Li+ Distribution in NMC811
content: A key challenge in 3D SIMS analysis is achieving optimal depth and lateral resolution. Conventional top-down SIMS depth profiling excels in depth resolution for flat, multi-layered structures, but suffers from limited lateral resolution, especially when analyzing the uneven surfaces commonly found on electrode active particle materials. Uneven sputtering can lead to inaccurate results due to differential top-down FIB milling, a limitation that is particularly significant for complex material structures in materials science. Optimizing lithium-ion battery (LIB) performance depends significantly on understanding the distribution of lithium ions (Li⁺) within the cathode active material. While energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) has been the primary technique for analyzing LIB cathode materials, it struggles to detect light elements such as lithium (Li) and boron (B). Secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) offers a superior alternative, providing exceptional sensitivity for light elements and making it ideal for characterizing Li⁺ distribution in LIBs.
